metadata.title: React Project Setup with Vite and Material Design

story.iWant: to set up a React 18 SPA with Vite, TypeScript, routing, and Material Design 3
story.soThat: I have a solid foundation for building UI components

tasks.task: Configure TypeScript for strict type safety (AC: #2)
Install and configure React Router v6 (AC: #3)
Apply Clarity Enterprise Design System theme customization (AC: #5)
Create folder structure and placeholder components (AC: #6)
Install and configure ESLint and Prettier (AC: #7)
Set up public folder with favicon and metadata (AC: #8)
Configure environment variables for dev and prod (AC: #9)
Test build and dev server startup (AC: #10, #11)
Create comprehensive README with setup instructions (AC: #11)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: React 18 project created with Vite (npm create vite@latest cicsgenapp-frontend -- --template react-ts)
TypeScript configured for type safety (tsconfig.json with strict mode enabled)
React Router v6 configured for client-side routing (BrowserRouter, Routes, lazy loading)
Material-UI (MUI) v5 installed with TypeScript support
Clarity Enterprise Design System theme customization applied (color palette, typography)
Project structure created with 7 primary folders (components, pages, services, hooks, context, types, styles)
ESLint and Prettier configured for code style
Public folder with favicon, index.html, robots.txt
Build process tested: npm run build (optimized build, size < 500KB gzipped for JavaScript bundle)

doc.title: Epic Breakdown - EPIC 3: React Frontend - Authentication & Core UI
doc.section: Story 3.1: React Project Setup with Vite and Material Design
doc.snippet: As a Frontend Developer, I want to set up a React 18 SPA with Vite, TypeScript, routing, and Material Design 3, So that I have a solid foundation for building UI components. Acceptance Criteria includes Vite setup, TypeScript strict mode, React Router v6, Material-UI v5, Clarity theme, project structure, ESLint/Prettier, build optimization.

doc.title: Development Guide
doc.snippet: Development guide for setting up local frontend development environment, including Node.js LTS requirements, npm/yarn setup, and development server configuration for React applications.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: PRD defines frontend technology stack: React 18, Vite, TypeScript, Material-UI v5, React Router v6, responsive design, accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA), and performance targets.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Architecture documentation includes frontend patterns for component layering, state management with React Context, API integration patterns, and design system integration with Material-UI.

doc.title: Data Models
doc.snippet: Data models document includes TypeScript interfaces for Customer, Policy, User, and other domain entities that will be used in frontend components and API responses.

doc.title: Story 2.8: API Documentation and Audit Logging
doc.snippet: Story 2.8 documents API response format (data/metadata wrapper), error handling patterns, authentication model (JWT bearer tokens from Zitadel), and correlation ID usage. Frontend must consume these patterns.

artifact.reason: Frontend development depends on backend API availability; review backend dependencies and versions for compatibility, especially Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, and auth patterns.
Frontend will call customer REST endpoints; understand request/response schemas, authentication requirements, and error handling patterns used in this controller.
Stories 2.1-2.8 define customer API endpoints, response formats, and validation rules that frontend will consume via API calls.

package.name: axios
package.reason: HTTP client for API calls (to be added in Story 3.8)

constraint.rule: All code must use TypeScript strict mode enabled (strict: true in tsconfig.json). No 'any' types except where explicitly justified.
Components must follow folder structure: src/components/ for reusable, src/pages/ for route-level components, src/hooks/ for custom hooks, src/context/ for providers.
Use React Router v6 with lazy loading via React.lazy() and Suspense for code splitting. All routes must have proper error boundaries.
Apply Clarity Enterprise Design System colors and typography via MUI theme provider. Do not hardcode colors; use theme values.
Use VITE_ prefix for environment variables (Vite convention). Store in .env.dev, .env.prod, .env.example. Load via import.meta.env.
Optimize build output to < 500KB gzipped JavaScript bundle. Use lazy loading and code splitting to achieve target.
Dev server must run on http://localhost:3000 (or configurable in vite.config.ts). Backend API expected at http://localhost:8080 (configurable via VITE_API_BASE_URL).
ESLint and Prettier must be configured and run as pre-commit hooks to prevent unformatted code commits.
Test framework (Jest + React Testing Library) setup deferred to Story 3.7 (Form Components). For now, ensure project structure supports tests/ directory.
Pin major versions of key dependencies (React 18, TypeScript 5, MUI 5) in package.json. Use npm ci for reproducible installs in CI/CD.

interface.name: API Base URL Configuration
interface.description: Frontend must know backend API base URL for all REST calls. Configured via environment variables and loaded at runtime.

interface.name: Zitadel OIDC Configuration
interface.description: Authentication configuration for Zitadel OIDC provider (Story 3.2 will implement). Configured via environment variables.

interface.name: Theme Provider
interface.description: Material-UI ThemeProvider must wrap the entire application to apply custom theme globally. Theme defined in src/theme/theme.ts.

interface.name: Router Configuration
interface.signature: BrowserRouter, Routes, Route from react-router-dom - top-level routing
interface.description: React Router v6 must be configured at application root. Routes defined in src/router/Router.tsx with lazy loading via React.lazy().

interface.name: Project Structure Layout
interface.description: Standard React project structure with clear separation: reusable components, page components, services, custom hooks, context providers, TypeScript types, styling, utilities, routing, and configuration.

tests.standards: Testing will be implemented in later stories (3.7 for form components). For Story 3.1, verification is manual: (1) npm run dev starts dev server on http://localhost:3000, (2) npm run build completes without errors and produces bundle < 500KB gzipped, (3) vite.config.ts and tsconfig.json configured correctly, (4) ESLint and Prettier run without errors on src/ folder.

locations.location: src/tests/ - Test directory (to be created in Story 3.7)
src/ - Jest/RTL tests will follow pattern: __tests__/ subdirectory or *.test.tsx files alongside source
e2e/ - End-to-end tests via Playwright/Cypress (future epic)

ideas.idea: Verify Vite project initializes with React 18 and TypeScript strict mode enabled
Verify tsconfig.json has all strict options enabled: strict: true, noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, noUnusedLocals, etc.
Verify React Router v6 routes can be navigated without page reload; check Network tab for lazy loading
Verify Material-UI components render correctly (Button, TextField, Card, etc.)
Verify Clarity theme colors applied correctly (primary blue #0050D8, secondary gray #6A7781, etc.)
Verify project folder structure matches requirements: src/components/, src/pages/, src/services/, src/hooks/, src/context/, src/types/, src/styles/
Verify ESLint and Prettier run without errors; npm run lint and npm run format work correctly
Verify public folder includes favicon, index.html with proper meta tags, robots.txt
Verify environment variables loaded correctly: console.log(import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL) shows correct value
Verify npm run build completes without errors; check dist/ folder size (should be < 500KB gzipped)
Verify dev server runs on http://localhost:3000; can navigate to routes and see hot module replacement working
